alternatives.tradeoff: One directory per content; two installations under different terms cannot both be represented and archiving would take the notices.
Cheaper; two installs differing in tokenizer become indistinguishable.
No staging space; a failure mid-write leaves a corrupt live model.

decisions.consequences: Installation needs space for staged, stored and materialized copies, checked first; hashing is a visible step; a runtime update changes the recorded revision on new runs.
decisions.reconsider_when: Hashing time becomes a usability problem, or a model kind's descriptor does not fit the per-kind pattern.

decisions.title: Meetings: host-time alignment, SpeakerKit diarization in its own service, channel origin as fact
decisions.choice: Two artifacts aligned in production by the per-stream measured-rate estimator, with recordings above the residual bound marked alignment_degraded; diarization behind a port in its own service with download disabled, explicit model folder and concurrency recorded in the manifest; whole-input operation only where F5 measures it flat, otherwise 10-minute windows with 30-second overlap through the staging artifact in D-043; confidence stored as unknown with centroid distance proposing identity for confirmation; notes as a separate run with per-bullet citations.
decisions.rationale: The requirement asks for an explicit runtime and editable names, and the documented configuration flags are what keep acquisition controlled, which is also why it has its own service. Alignment needs an observable that exists in a real meeting, so buffer host timestamps are used rather than reference tones, which cannot be injected into a user's meeting and whose fixture-derived rate would not describe their hardware. Evidence is represented at the boundary the cited declaration supports.

alternatives.tradeoff: Direct ground truth; requires injecting audible markers or reusing a fixture rate that does not describe the user's devices.

alternatives.option: Whole-input diarization with no duration contract
alternatives.tradeoff: Best clustering; leaves the memory behavior of the longest input unspecified.
One capture path; discards the channel signal.

alternatives.option: Apply cross-recording identity above a threshold
alternatives.tradeoff: Less user work; the SDK defines no universal threshold.

decisions.consequences: Two native-rate artifacts per meeting; weights are an explicit acquisition step; windowing can split a speaker across a boundary until merged, at a measured frequency; unverified attribution is the normal state; if measured error or correction cost exceeds range the default becomes channel labels with diarization user-enablable.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows flat whole-input operation, exposes per-segment evidence, or evaluation calibrates centroid distance.

decisions.title: History: append-only results over identified runs, full-text search, tombstones with generations
decisions.choice: Recordings expand into runs and result chains; search is FTS5 over result text excluding retained context; reprocessing inserts a run and results with a user-movable displayed-run pointer; deletion tombstones, increments a generation and signals cancellation, and every worker commits in one transaction that aborts on a missing, tombstoned or re-generated row.
decisions.rationale: A late response cannot recreate a deleted recording only if the check and the insert are one transaction, and the generation covers delete-then-recreate at one identifier. Organizing by run is what makes reprocessing comparable, since each run names its inputs, models and code revisions.

alternatives.option: Hard delete and let workers fail
alternatives.tradeoff: No bookkeeping; a constraint violation becomes the race outcome and scratch is orphaned.
No tombstone state; a hung worker blocks the delete indefinitely.
Simpler list; comparing a new model against the old becomes impossible.

decisions.consequences: Deleted recordings hold disk until leases release, so the interface says deleting; FTS triggers must handle deletion; multi-run recordings need a detail view making inputs and outputs obvious.
decisions.reconsider_when: Result rows dominate database size.

decisions.title: Menu bar surface, software input gain, and automatic resumption only under a verifiable continuity token
decisions.choice: A status item for state, mode, recent results and settings; software gain by default with metering and clipping indication and opt-in hardware volume restored only on an unchanged value; two adapter levels, where automatic resumption requires an observed playing-to-paused transition after the app's command plus an unchanged continuity token of player launch identity, item identity and playback position read again at resume; controlling-only adapters and unsupported players get manual actions only.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires an integration that identifies the player and confirms the pause, and says opting in does not remove that condition; ownership must also survive until the resume, and notification delivery is not guaranteed, so resting on stream completeness would assert a property no adapter supplies. A token read at both ends carries the claim with evidence, and posting the media key automatically is excluded because a toggle can start a paused player while an unrelated client keeps the device active.

alternatives.option: Trust an observed notification stream with gap detection
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler adapters; a missed notification is undetectable, so ownership rests on completeness nothing guarantees.

alternatives.option: Poll and resume if still paused
alternatives.tradeoff: Works with any state-reading adapter; cannot distinguish an untouched pause from a play and re-pause.
Per-application state without adapters; undocumented and breakable.
Nothing to get wrong; leaves background audio in recordings.

decisions.consequences: Automatic resume covers only players with a readable token, so coverage is narrow and grows per integration, with the menu showing each level; a stated residual is a play and re-pause returning to the identical item and position.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported API supplies player identity, pause confirmation and change notification.

decisions.title: Distinct toggle and push-to-talk bindings with evidence-based stuck-key recovery
decisions.choice: One consuming session event tap handling keyDown, keyUp and flagsChanged; separate bindings validated at bind time; push-to-talk finalizing on keyUp with optional tap-to-lock; recovery from tap-disabled, lock and sleep notifications plus a 1 Hz key-state poll; no maximum duration; Carbon fallback without the tap.
decisions.rationale: Overloading one binding with a hold discriminator leaves the first hold window undefined. Polling the physical key addresses the real problem, an undelivered key-up, with evidence about that key, while a maximum-hold watchdog would truncate valid speech and act as the duration limit the specification prohibits.

alternatives.option: One binding with a hold discriminator
alternatives.tradeoff: One combination; undefined behavior in the first hold window.
No Accessibility requirement; no key-up, so push-to-talk cannot exist.
Stops a stuck key; truncates a long push-to-talk recording.

decisions.consequences: The app sits on the keyboard path, so the handler must stay fast or the tap is disabled by timeout, which the re-enable path monitors; users configure two shortcuts; the poll runs only during push-to-talk.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported API provides global hotkeys with key-up.

decisions.title: One declared budget covering residency, working data and the non-model floor
decisions.choice: 8 GB peak across app and services, counting model residency and declared working data per job, four slots with one occupant each unloaded after ten idle minutes, a 400 MB preview cap, a 200 MB non-model ceiling, and refusal at activation with the arithmetic shown and labeled measured or declared, overridable, including the interactive-minimum check in D-004.
decisions.rationale: The specification forbids artificial quotas and requires honest limits, which differs from ignoring the ceiling, since swap turns a latency problem into a system-wide stall. Counting only weights hides the quantity that grows with the work, and labeling the basis keeps a refusal computed from declared numbers from becoming an invisible limit.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler; the quantity scaling with input sits outside the budget.
Fastest where memory allows; drives the target into swap.
Adapts to real conditions; reacts after the stall starts.

decisions.consequences: First use after idle pays a load; diarization and notes run sequentially under declared numbers; a job exceeding its ceiling is terminated with the figure recorded; until descriptors exist the budget can be wrong in either direction, which the refusal says.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measured figures differ materially from declared ones, or the ceiling stops binding.

decisions.title: Egress control enforced by the service sandbox with no exception
decisions.choice: Inference and decoding run in services denied network access, with downloads confined to an explicitly invoked downloader on a host allowlist writing only to staging, runtimes constructed with acquisition disabled behind a build check, and an external decoder shipped only under F2 child confinement; no setting runs user audio through an unconfined process.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires audio, transcripts and context to stay on the Mac, and RESEARCH notes a runtime that may download by default and states that a symbol scan cannot establish a lack of network access. Consent cannot convert a hard requirement into a preference, and an in-service decoder satisfies both the requirement and the request for an extension mechanism.

alternatives.option: External decoder with disclosed trust transfer
alternatives.tradeoff: Any format works; the process handling the user's audio is unconstrained.

alternatives.option: Unsandboxed service with a narrowed claim
alternatives.tradeoff: Any runtime usable; the offline property rests on rejected evidence.

alternatives.option: Allow runtimes to fetch missing models
alternatives.tradeoff: Better first run; makes network access a side effect of loading.

decisions.consequences: Entitlements are part of the signed product and fail closed; a runtime that cannot load inside the boundary is not shipped for that kind; without child confinement, adding a format is development work; container writes are not egress.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a required kind has no adapter inside the boundary, which is a product-owner question.

decisions.title: Runs as the provenance spine with a dependency table naming non-result inputs
decisions.choice: Every result belongs to a run, names its primary input where its kind has one, and records other inputs in result_dependencies including assignment revisions and audio artifacts; invariants are per result kind; results are immutable after insert.
decisions.rationale: A recording cannot have exactly one transcript while remaining re-recognizable, so parentage is a foreign key. A result-typed column could not name an assignment revision, leaving notes provenance nothing to point at, and two kinds legitimately have no textual parent, which is why a single invariant would fail on a correct diarization result.

alternatives.option: Single parent with other inputs in the manifest
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer rows; provenance queries cannot join, so History parses manifests.

alternatives.option: Fixed nullable columns per input kind
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper joins; a new result kind needs a migration.
No new table; breaks whenever runs overlap.

decisions.consequences: More joins and a run-oriented detail view; the invariant suite has one case per kind, which is the only satisfiable form; search can return two recognitions of one recording, disambiguated by result rows.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users never re-recognize or re-diarize, though the same structure makes translations and notes attributable.

decisions.title: Crash-safe capture with full packet-table accounting and idempotent finalization
decisions.choice: The journal layout, head, data and seal record formats including priming frames, per-chunk source frames and per-packet sizes, the sealer cycle, finalization order and recovery rule defined once in the data lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: Encoded bytes are fsynced before the record naming them, so recovery never builds a table over data that never reached disk. Packet sizes are recorded because a table cannot be rebuilt from a count and an offset, and frame counts are recorded because sizes alone do not describe the exact valid duration, which matters because the PCM is deleted as soon as its bytes are durable.

alternatives.tradeoff: Smaller records; recovery cannot reconstruct valid and trimmed duration after the PCM is gone.

alternatives.option: Treat a present pakt chunk as the commit signal
alternatives.tradeoff: No extra record; a torn table write is indistinguishable from a complete one.
No journal or extra fsyncs; recovery rests on an untested property of a format storing its table at the end.

decisions.consequences: Two fsyncs per chunk period per stream plus three in finalization, an idempotent recovery path F3 tests, and roughly a 30-second window of journal files beside the artifact; the fallback is retaining chunks until the artifact decodes and hashes.
decisions.reconsider_when: F3 shows an unacceptable bound, or a container with an incrementally durable index removes the need.

decisions.title: State-indexed recovery with an explicit durability ordering rule
decisions.choice: Every non-terminal state has an authoritative transition, listed once in the data lifecycle, with pre-commit disposition honored from the session manifest; recovery completes deterministic stages and never resumes generation, diarization or delivery without user action.
decisions.rationale: A sweep covering only some states leaves the rest to whichever test author reaches them first, which is the deferral the specification prohibits, and naming the ordering rule makes new stages easy to place. Recording disposition in the manifest is what makes a cancellation issued before the History row exists survive a crash.

alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; throws away a completed recognition after a crash during a rewrite.
Least friction; re-runs unwanted generation and risks delivering into whatever is focused.

alternatives.option: Ask the user per run at launch
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; invites blind dismissal.

decisions.consequences: A crashed meeting leaves a Generate action or resumable staging rather than new output, and behavior tables must cover every state for the crash suite to assert against.
decisions.reconsider_when: A stage appears whose effects are neither externally visible nor idempotent.

decisions.title: Permissions as a capability-by-state matrix
decisions.choice: The matrix over capability, run state and active adapter in the failure behavior section, with defined effects for denial, revocation and restoration.
decisions.rationale: Mapping every revocation to a capture failure would end a valid recording because a delivery permission changed during recognition, and would report a lost shortcut permission as an audio failure; capabilities serve different stages.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simple; stops valid work and misreports the cause.
No mid-run interruption; a later failure disconnected from the user's change.

decisions.consequences: The matrix is longer than a rule, directly testable and part of the approved tables; each capability needs a probe and a notification path; Accessibility loss mid-delivery holds rather than posting blind.
decisions.reconsider_when: A capability's loss needs a dimension beyond adapter identity.

decisions.title: Two lease scopes after commit, session-directory ownership before it, reclamation by liveness
decisions.choice: Artifact leases scoped to a recording and model leases scoped to a setHash with their distinct eligibility rules, holders and reclamation rule defined in the data lifecycle, with pre-commit ownership held by the session directory and its manifest disposition.
decisions.rationale: Model use needs its own eligibility because installation, its smoke test and live preview happen before any recording row exists, and a session directory cannot establish ownership of a shared model cache; keying the model lease to the setHash and installation state lets installation checks and pre-capture work participate. Defining staleness by holder liveness keeps a suspended app or a stalled worker from having its artifact deleted underneath it.

alternatives.option: One scope requiring a recording row
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; installation, smoke tests and preview have no recording to name, so they bypass the protocol or invent a row.
Recovers any stall; deletes an artifact a live but delayed holder is using.
One mechanism; History gains rows for recordings that may never exist.

decisions.consequences: Every consumer acquires the lease matching its scope, including playback, preview and cache deletion; recovery has two ownership paths to test; a wedged live holder blocks retention, which is reported rather than forced.
decisions.reconsider_when: Lease contention delays retention enough to matter.

decisions.title: Measurements precede the boundaries they can invalidate
decisions.choice: Five gates run before the boundaries depending on them, each with its range, basis and failure action approved before it runs; F2's child-confinement result is a shipping condition; gates govern shipped defaults only.
decisions.rationale: Several decisions depend on unmeasured properties, and scheduling them after the ports and schema built on them would let a negative result invalidate that work. A range with its basis and action is what makes a result decide something, and two gates produce shipped data rather than a verdict, which is stated so their absence is not read as failure.

alternatives.option: Start the skeleton and measure later
alternatives.tradeoff: Visible progress sooner; a negative result forces rework of the port, scheduler, writer or meeting schema.
Avoids arguing thresholds in advance; invites fitting the threshold to the result.

alternatives.option: Accept the unknowns as implementation risks
alternatives.tradeoff: No gates; hands behavioral decisions to whichever task hits them.

decisions.consequences: Some work produces evidence rather than shippable behavior, including a measurement-only harness, and the decisions fed by gates carry conservative defaults until evidence lands.
decisions.reconsider_when: A gate's fallback proves acceptable enough that the measurement is not worth its cost.

decisions.title: Named approval authority, traceability, and approved ranges with recorded basis
decisions.choice: Behavior tables cite SPEC.md clauses or are marked derived, the approver is the user as product owner or a named delegate, and the same approver signs gate ranges with basis and failure action before each gate, rubric rules before scoring, and the pre-effect class and profiles before either licenses a fallthrough; a missed range returns to the approver rather than being dropped by engineering.
decisions.rationale: A passing test proves only that code met its assertions, so assertions need an owner. Ranges are approved because they decide which runtime and defaults ship, and each carries its basis so a derived criterion is distinguishable from an invented one; the delivery class and profiles are the shipped data that can license a second write into another application.

alternatives.tradeoff: Cheap; two people can share a misreading with nobody empowered to settle it.
Less owner time; a missed target could be discarded by the party it constrains.
No second artifact; it does not enumerate state and event pairs, so implementers fill gaps silently.

decisions.consequences: Acceptance, gates and fallthrough data all wait on approval, putting the owner on the critical path in three places, while derived rows and unbased ranges stay visible as categories.
decisions.reconsider_when: Approval becomes the dominant delay, arguing for pre-approved templates.

decisions.title: Direct Developer ID distribution, ad hoc signing for local builds
decisions.choice: Ship outside the Mac App Store, notarized with the hardened runtime, as an unsandboxed shell containing sandboxed services; App Store submission is not planned.
decisions.rationale: The specification settles this in substance: it asks for direct distribution for this example and requires a consuming event tap with key-up and selected-text insertion into other applications, neither available to a sandboxed App Store build.

alternatives.tradeoff: System updates and a familiar install; the sandbox removes push-to-talk and accessibility insertion.
No certificate cost; Gatekeeper blocks casual installation and TCC grants become fragile.
Reach plus capability; two feature sets and test matrices.

decisions.consequences: Updates need their own mechanism and release packaging carries certificates and notarization; ad hoc builds have unstable identity, so permission grants are re-requested and developers keep a stably signed build.
decisions.reconsider_when: A product decision requires App Store presence, which would require revising Text delivery and Recording controls first.

decisions.title: Notes as a separate run pinning assignments over versioned derived segments, with carried assignments unverified
decisions.choice: The revision chain, derived segments, attribution states, the assigned_by_user invariant, overlap carry-forward as unverified proposals and the notes run's pinned inputs, defined in the data lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: Notes depend on user-editable data, so the snapshot rule extends to assignments, splits and names, and starting the run after its inputs commit makes the pin real. Splitting needs its own representation because mapping source segments to identities leaves a split nowhere to live. Carrying an assignment into new boundaries by time overlap is an inference rather than the user's act, so treating it as assigned_by_user would let a guess inherit the evidentiary status the meeting design withholds elsewhere.

alternatives.tradeoff: No re-confirmation work; an overlap guess becomes indistinguishable from a user assignment and appears in notes.
One segment table; model output stops being immutable and citations become unresolvable.
Simplest schema; a merged-speaker segment leaves the user no correction.
Always current; silently replaces text the user relied on.

decisions.consequences: A meeting produces at least two runs, speaker edits write small revisions deleted with the recording, a crash before the notes run leaves a Generate action, and after re-diarization the user confirms proposals rather than finding assignments applied.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows overlap-based proposals are usually wrong, which would drop carry-forward.

decisions.title: Installation lifecycle states bound storage when a runtime is replaced
decisions.choice: States installed, archived, orphaned_runtime and missing; archiving clears one installation's claim while retaining row, hashes, capabilities and notices, with History rendering from params_rendered and reprocessing refused with a restore offer; adapter removal deletes nothing; physical release follows the single retention invariant; the manager reports retained bytes and, at install time, what a replacement adds and archiving releases.
decisions.rationale: Reference counting cannot bound storage because results reference installations permanently, so separating what persists for attribution from what persists for execution is what makes the bound achievable. Because adapter removal deletes nothing, storage stays held until the user acts, so the numbers are surfaced rather than left theoretical.

alternatives.option: Retain assets for any referenced installation
alternatives.tradeoff: Reprocessing always available; storage grows without bound.
Bounded automatically; destroys reprocessing on a build change the user did not make.

alternatives.option: Archive automatically by age or size
alternatives.tradeoff: No user decision; removes reprocessing without warning.

decisions.consequences: Four states appear in the manager and History, restoring requires the same assets by manifest hash, and missing is distinguished from archived so an unexpected disappearance reads as an error.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users archive and restore the same installations repeatedly.

decisions.title: Retained context as an owned artifact with a stated lifetime
decisions.choice: Opt-in retention stores the sample as a file with a row naming run, recording, source kind, representation, path, length and hash, fsynced before the row, deleted with the recording and by retention, and excluded from the index; otherwise only a digest exists.
decisions.rationale: Promising retained context while the schema listed digests only would leave owner, deletion and migration to whichever task first stored a string, which is the deferral the specification prohibits for persistent data. Files rather than columns because recognition output can be large and deletion then rides on directory removal.

alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer file kind; large samples inflate the database and its migrations.
Search finds surrounding material; returns hits in text the user never spoke.
Least storage; reprocessing cannot reproduce an original result even when wanted.

decisions.consequences: Retention appears in the size view and per-recording detail, the mode editor states the cost, and protection is the file system's.
decisions.reconsider_when: A threat model asks for at-rest encryption, applying to the whole library.

decisions.title: Materialized caches are content-owned store artifacts under one retention invariant
decisions.choice: The service copies assets into materialized/<setHash>/, verifies every asset against the installation manifest, then writes and fsyncs a marker; the app registers materialized_assets keyed by (set_hash, service_kind); retention, release, sweeps and lease participation follow the single invariant in the data lifecycle, and adapter removal deletes nothing.
decisions.rationale: The third access mechanism keeps the egress boundary exception-free, and an unowned copy would reintroduce the problem D-038 solves in a place no accounting enumerates. Keying by content matches the content-addressed path: two installations of identical bytes share one copy, so an installation-keyed deletion rule would let archiving one remove the cache the other is using. The marker gives crash recovery a signal independent of size comparison, and the materialization lease gives an in-progress copy an owner before its marker and row exist.

alternatives.option: Key the cache and deletion by installation
alternatives.tradeoff: One owner per copy; installations sharing content share one path, so archiving one deletes the other's cache.

alternatives.option: Treat the copy as private service state
alternatives.tradeoff: No table or sweep; gigabytes accumulate outside the storage bound and the size report.
Nothing persists; every run pays a multi-gigabyte copy dominating first-token latency.
No second copy; a confined process following the link is still confined, so this is a path exception renamed.

decisions.consequences: A runtime needing materialization doubles its footprint, shown in the manager and checked at activation; verification adds a hash pass; a crashed copy costs at most one sweep interval.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows no runtime needs materialization, or descriptor loading appears upstream.

decisions.title: Local model import identity when provenance metadata is absent
decisions.choice: Identity rests on the manifest hash; publisher, revision, licence identifiers and notices are optional, their absence recording provenance unknown or licence unknown with an editable label; nothing about missing metadata affects compatibility, the smoke test, activation or use, and the only consequence is that the downloader will not offer that asset.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires compatible user-supplied models to work and forbids an absent benchmark from disabling one, so an identity scheme needing publisher and revision would make missing metadata a compatibility gate by another route. Hashing the manifest gives complete identity from the bytes, so labels can be decoration; the download restriction limits what the app offers, not what the user runs.

alternatives.tradeoff: Readable identity; a compatible directory cannot be installed without invented metadata.
Every asset has recorded terms; the user's own model becomes unusable on a paperwork condition.
Sets expectations; reads as a capability limit on a model that works.

decisions.consequences: Two installations can be distinguished only by a hash prefix until renamed, so labels are editable and the hash is shown; notices keyed by installation mean an identical import keeps its own terms.
decisions.reconsider_when: Unlabeled imports become common enough that hash prefixes dominate the interface.

decisions.title: Every model-bound job declares a working-data contract constant in input duration
decisions.choice: Each adapter publishes a ceiling expressed in parameters the app controls and never in input duration; speech and decoding satisfy it through credit windows with the decoder registration check, diarization through flat whole-input operation or the windowed contract in D-043, generation through context length and windowed notes; admission counts the ceiling, breaches terminate the job, and the long-input protocol samples every participating process with its own decode-path range and action.
decisions.rationale: The specification forbids memory proportional to decoded duration, and credit bounds a queue rather than a producer: a diarizer accumulating embeddings or a decoder buffering a file would break the requirement while every credit window stayed correct. Giving the decode path its own range means a buffering decoder is rejected before shipping rather than found during a user's import.

alternatives.tradeoff: One mechanism; says nothing about what a component holds internally.

alternatives.option: Measure only the app and speech service
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper; the least-known processes go unmeasured.
Bounds memory trivially; the specification forbids artificial limits.
One path and a guaranteed bound; pays cross-window identity cost where a runtime is measurably flat.

decisions.consequences: Adapters carry a descriptor field that must stay honest, a wrong declaration surfaces as a terminated job rather than swap, and process-level sampling replaces a single memory graph.
decisions.reconsider_when: A runtime exposes its own memory contract, or growth is bounded but not constant, needing a declared function.

decisions.title: Windowed diarization writes a run-owned staging artifact published in one transaction
decisions.choice: Window output and cluster centroids go to run-owned staging under the recording directory, fsynced per window and invisible to search and provenance; one transaction publishes the diarization result, segments, assignment revision 1 and derived segments, then deletes staging; cancellation deletes it, interruption retains it as resumable for the same run under its pinned manifest, recording deletion removes it and aborts the publish, and a sweep removes staging whose run is terminal and not resumable.
decisions.rationale: Committing rows per window would contradict the cancellation and recovery rules and leave a partial segment set indistinguishable from a complete one, while discarding window output would make a crash hours into a meeting cost the whole run. Staging separates durability from visibility, localizes the storage growth the specification allows, and gives cross-window cluster state a defined home and lifetime.

alternatives.tradeoff: Progress visible and resumable with no artifact; a cancelled or crashed run leaves a partial set that looks complete.
Nothing to sweep; a crash discards hours of work and cluster state grows in the process that must stay bounded.
The service owns its scratch; the store could not size, sweep or delete it with the recording.

alternatives.option: Publish incrementally into a hidden partial result
alternatives.tradeoff: One storage mechanism; a partial result is still a row search, provenance and notes can reach.

decisions.consequences: One more artifact kind with sweeps, size accounting and deletion rules; a resumed run stays attributable to the settings it started with; resume applies to interruption and not cancellation, which the panel states.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows the runtime accepts incremental input with resumable state, or whole-input operation measures flat.

coverage.explanation: A consuming session event tap gives global toggle and push-to-talk from another application as separate validated bindings with per-mode variants, available because of the distribution decision (D-036, D-026); lost key-up is recovered from notifications and a key-state poll, so there is no duration cap. Capture starts at the trigger into the pre-roll ring while arming runs concurrently (D-006). Without Accessibility or Input Monitoring, toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey and push-to-talk is unavailable with an explanation (D-032). Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage including sealing, diarizing and noting, with sealing returning immediately behind a durable disposition (D-007), and a crash resolves through the state-indexed recovery contract over the same stages (D-031).

The transcript is inserted at the caret or over the selection through AXSelectedText, never the element's value (D-009). One target is resolved per focus outcome and revalidated before every external effect, including the accessibility write, with a pre-effect mismatch ending as held and a later one as unconfirmed (D-008). Duplicate delivery is prevented by evidence-based fallthrough: a probe routes unsupported targets before any write, only approved pre-effect codes permit a next rung with messaging failures excluded, an unchanged readback is never a rejection, and typing needs an applicable unexpired profile. Submission posts Return only after confirmation and only if the text still sits where it was confirmed. Clipboard state is snapshotted and restored only on confirmation or user action. Permission loss and secure input route results to History and the clipboard (D-032), and no attempt rests in a state without a recovery transition (D-010).

A provisional live transcript and waveform appear in a non-activating panel that never becomes key and remembers placement fractionally with clamping when a display is gone (D-011). Provisional text is styled and labeled distinctly, replaced by the final transcript, and never persisted because it was produced over partial context and is a different artifact from the committed result (D-006). Failures appear as a panel row with a reason and one action. The ladder is executable rather than nominal because interactive runs reserve the speech-primary slot and preempt batch work across slots (D-004) and the preview model has its own capped slot counted with its working data (D-027), with stated latency, update, dropped-frame and paired non-inferiority criteria and no waveform-only end state.

Standard, Email, Note and Meeting notes cover ordinary dictation and task-specific output with permitted transformations enumerated per mode and summarization confined to Meeting notes under a citation requirement (D-013). All declare that they do not answer questions, and the claim is bounded by what the checks establish (D-012): an observed violation retries once and then delivers the normalized transcript while retaining the generated text marked contract_violation, and without a validator pack the rewrite is produced and retained while the delivered text is the normalized transcript, with no override, because a question-mark signal cannot show that no question was asked. The checks are necessary conditions, which is why the adversarial corpus and the monotone rubric decide whether a built-in ships.

Users author prompts and formatting rules, and each mode fills a structured contract the editor requires before saving (D-012). Modes select local speech and language models by content identity covering every behavior-affecting asset (D-022), computable for a user-built model with no publisher or licence metadata (D-041). Every save creates a content-addressed revision, and every run pins it with model installations, runtime, adapter and application pipeline revisions, vocabulary, language and validator packs (D-006), so work in progress reads its snapshot and a later edit cannot change a saved result's meaning; History shows the producing revision and diffs it. Results stay attributable through their run (D-029), and check coverage changes only whether a rewrite is delivered automatically, never which models may run.

Rules match bundle identifier and, where readable, URL, evaluated at arming with first match winning over a user-ordered list whose position is the entire precedence rule and whose shadowed entries are flagged (D-014). A predicate whose input cannot be obtained does not match and evaluation continues, so denied automation or screen recording narrows matching without disturbing capture (D-032); with no match the default applies. The mode is latched into the manifest so it cannot change mid-sentence, and the effective mode with its source appears in the panel and menu bar every run (D-011). Browser URL availability is a dated matrix, and an incomplete one degrades to bundle-identifier rules.

Terminology enters at four points in fixed order relative to recognition and language processing: prompt-slot biasing, deterministic replacement with longest-match and list-order precedence over the recognition result, a separate filler pass, and reapplication after generation (D-015). Biasing shifts decoding probabilities and the interface says so, with no claim that adding a name guarantees recognition, because the mechanism is a prompt rather than a constraint (D-020). Replacement is ICU-boundary-aware with a stated fallback for unspaced scripts, case-preserving and non-cascading, so implementations cannot diverge. Vocabulary survival is a language-independent check that runs with or without a pack (D-012), so a model normalizing an unusual proper noun is caught, and both texts are retained.

Active-application text, an opt-in screen frame through Vision, and pasteboard text are sampled at arming against a 200 ms deadline, capped, with omissions recorded (D-016). Context is data supplied to a mode: every source is distilled to a term list, removing instruction-shaped sentences rather than detecting them later, and a prose source additionally requires the language-dependent set to be available and to pass before automatic delivery, with the residual limit stated (D-012). Retention defaults to a digest, and opting in stores an owned artifact deleted with the recording (D-039). Every transient copy has a release point on every path, including runs with no generation stage. Missing permissions leave a named state (D-032), and context never leaves the machine because it crosses only into services the system denies network access, with no component excepted (D-028).

Recognition language is explicit or detected against a recorded threshold with a visible fallback below it (D-017). Translation into English is a separate declared operation naming the exact parent result it translated, so the source transcript is preserved and stays identifiable after re-recognition (D-029). Recognition, rewriting and translation are evaluated separately, translation being scored against the retained source transcript so recognition errors are charged to recognition. Compatibility is declared per installation and checked at activation, with language claims attributed to the publisher and marked unmeasured (D-022). Pack coverage restricts neither models nor languages; it changes only automatic delivery for a mode declaring it does not answer questions (D-012).

Microphone, system audio and imported audio and video implement one AudioSource emitting timestamped native frames with conversion as a later stage and credit bounding queues (D-018). The initial matrix is what system decoders cover, and the extension mechanism is a DecoderProvider as a confined child or inside the decode service, chosen by F2, with no setting that runs audio through an unconfined process (D-028). The memory requirement is met by a declared contract constant in duration plus per-process measurement and a decode-path range with a failure action, since credit bounds a queue and not a producer (D-042). Concurrency is bounded to one live session with seekable ingest in slots while live capture stays exempt (D-004). A failed import leaves its source unchanged because the path opens it read-only and commits only after completion (D-019).

Two streams are captured crash-safely (D-030) and aligned in production by the per-stream measured-rate estimator, with recordings above the residual bound marked alignment_degraded (D-023). Channel origin is recorded as a capture fact rather than speaker identity. Diarization has a named runtime in its own sandboxed service with acquisition disabled, is a run stage with cancellation, recovery and admission (D-006, D-027), and carries a duration contract: flat whole-input operation or bounded windows whose output lives in a run-owned staging artifact published in one transaction, never as partial rows (D-042, D-043). Evidence is represented at the boundary the cited declaration supports, with confidence unknown and centroid distance proposing identity for confirmation. Assigning, merging, splitting and renaming append revisions over versioned derived segments, carried assignments after re-diarization are unverified proposals, and notes are a separate run pinning transcript, diarization result, assignment revision and names, citing derived segment ranges and dropping uncited bullets (D-037). Quality is reported with components separated plus segment-level and correction-cost measures that decide a default rather than availability.

Recordings are searchable through FTS5 over result text and playable from the sealed artifact (D-005, D-024). Each recording expands into runs and result chains, so reprocessing through another model or mode inserts new runs and results while earlier results stay immutable and attributable, with each naming its inputs, mode revision, installations and code revisions (D-029). Deletion during active processing tombstones, increments a generation and signals cancellation, and every worker commits in one transaction that aborts on a missing, tombstoned or re-generated row, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording; deletion before the sealing commit is a manifest disposition (D-033). Retention policies are ordinary deletion jobs under the same leases, and discarding audio disables playback and re-recognition while text reprocessing remains. Interrupted work resolves through the recovery contract covering diarizing and noting (D-031), and space reads as deleting until the last lease releases.

The library browses and manages speech, preview, language and diarization installations with capabilities, sizes, notices and owning runtime (D-022). Identity hashes every behavior-affecting asset and each run also records runtime, adapter and application pipeline revisions. Because identity is computable from bytes, a compatible local model imports and activates with no publisher, licence or benchmark metadata, labeled provenance unknown and unmeasured, and the only consequence is that the app will not offer those assets for download (D-041). Compatibility and smoke tests are per kind and never quality judgments. Installation stages, verifies, tests, writes notices, renames and commits in one transaction, so a failed download or import cannot replace a working installation. Loading never downloads: absolute paths, prohibited downloading initializers, an explicitly invoked downloader and network-denied services (D-003, D-028, D-023). Replacing a runtime has bounded interface and storage effect: separate adapter targets and descriptors (D-002, D-020, D-021), rows rendering from params_rendered, adapter removal deleting nothing, archiving releasing blobs and caches once no claim remains under one retention invariant, and caches registered, verified, lease-aware and swept (D-038, D-040). Activation over budget is refused with the arithmetic shown, labeled measured or declared, and overridable (D-027).

A menu bar status item shows state, effective mode, recent results and settings alongside the recording panel (D-011, D-025). Microphone level adjustment is software gain by default with metering and clipping indication, so the common case changes no system state; hardware volume is opt-in and restored only when the current value still equals what the app set, with a mismatch leaving it as found. Media control is confined to what the app can own over time: an adapter identifies the player and pauses it, and automatic resumption additionally requires an observed pause transition plus an unchanged continuity token read again at resume, because a query-only adapter cannot distinguish an untouched pause from a play and re-pause and notification streams are not guaranteed complete. Players without that evidence get manual actions only, and the media key is never posted automatically because it can start a paused player while an unrelated client keeps the device active. Losing automation removes that adapter (D-032), and the APIs these behaviors use sit under the baseline in D-001 with availability checks and defined fallbacks.

open_questions.question: Which access mechanism does each runtime need inside a network-denied sandboxed service, and is a child of DecodeService confined?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F2 before entitlements, the access path and the decoder extension freeze. The boundary is fixed either way: a runtime loading under none of the three is replaced by the alternative adapter, and an unconfined child means the external decoder is not built and formats are added inside the service. Only a model kind with no adapter that loads inside the boundary reaches the product owner.

open_questions.question: Which accessibility error codes, if any, are returned only before the target applied the write?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F4 populates the approved class per code, target and version; it ships empty and permanently excludes messaging failures and timeouts. The ladder does not wait, because the settability probe already routes unsupported targets and an unclassified error ends the attempt as unconfirmed with the transcript on the pasteboard. A permanently empty class costs one click in rare cases.

open_questions.question: How does the shipping speech runtime behave on long input and under cancellation, and does it meet accuracy, latency and memory ranges?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F1 with ranges, bases and actions approved first, including an absolute acceptance basis so a comparison alone cannot pass two unusable transcribers. Failure promotes the measurement harness to a shipping adapter, changes the default pairing, or returns the latency question to the approver.

open_questions.question: How much audio is lost on an abrupt kill, does finalization survive a crash at every write, and does the rebuilt table trim correctly?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F3 asserts a maximum lost interval, decoded valid frame count and trimming against retained reference PCM, and convergence of repeated recovery, plus the backlog under contention. Failure shortens the chunk period, adopts retain-until-verified, or reduces ingest slots and raises encode priority.

open_questions.question: Which targets support selected-text insertion with a preserved field, allow the predicate to be evaluated, and expose a rejection signal, at which versions?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F4's dated matrix, which scopes profiles and their expiry. The ladder does not wait: with no applicable profile, typing is unreachable and an uncertain outcome is unconfirmed with the transcript left on the pasteboard.

open_questions.question: Which fields does the pinned diarizer expose, does it accept incremental input, and does its service hold memory proportional to meeting duration?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F5. The schema already stores unknown where the declaration establishes nothing, and the structural fallback needs no unavailable capability: 10-minute windows with overlap through the staging artifact and centroid matching, whose identity cost is then measured. No centroid means cross-recording naming is a user action with no proposal.

open_questions.question: Do the initial media player adapters expose a continuity token that shows no playback change intervened?
open_questions.resolution: Confirm per player during implementation against the manual matrix including a play-and-repause between pause and resume. A confirmed token ships the adapter as observing; otherwise it ships controlling-only, pausing and offering manual resume. Coverage is a measured list rather than a promise.

open_questions.question: Which languages get validator packs at ship, and how often does a missing pack withhold automatic delivery from users who wanted the rewrite?
open_questions.resolution: Ship the English pack with the first generation modes and add packs driven by measured checks_partial and one-click delivery rates. No model or language is blocked meanwhile, and a mode intended for an unpacked language can be authored as a revision declaring that it answers questions, which the indicator shows.

open_questions.question: Which browsers expose the current URL, and which need automation permission or provide nothing?
open_questions.resolution: A dated per-browser table before URL rules ship; an unreadable URL is a non-match, so an incomplete table degrades to bundle-identifier rules and the default mode.

open_questions.question: Is FTS5 compiled into the system SQLite on the baseline?
open_questions.resolution: A runtime check during store setup; if absent, build GRDB against a bundled SQLite, accepting a larger binary and an update obligation, recorded against D-005.

open_questions.question: Is an 8B-class instruct model at 4-bit the right default for Email and Meeting notes now that preview, diarization and working data share the budget?
open_questions.resolution: Score two or three sizes against the fidelity corpus under the approved rubric, pair the result with the F5 footprint, the preview slot and declared ceilings, and pick a default that fits with meetings running. Model selection is per mode, so a wrong default is a settings change.

open_questions.question: Which diarization weight assets may be offered for download rather than only imported?
open_questions.resolution: Compile the notice inventory per asset against the component-specific references, storing each notice under the acquiring installation so archiving cannot remove it. The feature ships either way, because weights are user-acquired and an asset without redistribution terms stays importable with licence unknown.
